# VideoScan — how the data is organized (schema 14; written 2026-10-31, tables regenerated 2026-11-01)

*Rick's ask (2026-10-31): "a PDF of the database fields and organization of the data so I can read it and know how it is organized." Generated by `tools/data_organization.py` from the live catalog read-only — table names, columns and row counts only, no family data. Regenerate after a migration.*

Status: built — 2026-11-01. The file map (the `#` sections, Rick's text) is maintained by hand; the tables between the markers are regenerated by `tools/data_organization.py` from the live catalog, read-only. Schema 14 since 2026-11-01 (v14 `provenance_assertions`); the tables below were regenerated on 2026-11-01 from a sqlite `.backup` copy of the migrated live catalog (64 tables).

## Where every file of this app lives on the system

*Rick (2026-10-31): "we must write down WHERE all files related to this app live in the system." Inventory taken on `RicksUltra` on 2026-10-31. One file per line; sizes are that day's. Paths and file names only — no family data; the repo is public. Which Swift file writes each one is in the first edition of this doc (commit `e11fa248`) if it is ever needed. A new file name under App Support fails `AppSupportSideStoreInventoryTests` until it is classified there.*

**Short names used in the Where column**

| Short | Full path |
|---|---|
| `AppSupport/` | `~/Library/Application Support/VideoScan/` |
| `Logs/` | `~/Library/Logs/VideoScan/` |
| `Caches/` | `~/Library/Caches/` |
| `repo/` | `~/dev/VideoScan/` (same path on every Mac) |
| `defaults` | domain `Rick-Breen.VideoScan` = `~/Library/Preferences/Rick-Breen.VideoScan.plist` |

**Who writes** — `app` = VideoScan.app (its committer is the only catalog writer); `helper` = VideoScan Background; `findtagd` / `previewsweepd` = the two daemons; `script` = a repo script or tool; `Rick` = by hand; `frozen` = imported, never written again.

# POI (The People Tab)

The catalog keeps only `people_tags` (digest, name, kind, provenance); who the people ARE lives here.

| File | Where | What it is | Who writes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POI/<profile-UUID>/profile.json` | `AppSupport/POI/` | one person of interest: name, aliases, reference list (13 profiles, 207 MB) | app |
| `POI/<profile-UUID>/*.jpeg`, `*.jpg`, `*.png` | `AppSupport/POI/` | that person's reference face crops and chosen photos | app |
| `POI/<profile-UUID>/profile.json.pre-*` | `AppSupport/POI/` | pre-repair copies of a profile | app |
| `POI/.uuid-migration.json` | `AppSupport/POI/` | the name → UUID migration record | app |
| `POI/Families/<family-UUID>.json` | `AppSupport/POI/Families/` | family groupings of profiles; the About People list reads these | app |
| `POI/poi-m1.txt` | `AppSupport/POI/` | a note from the M1 sync (2026-09) | Rick |
| `personfinder_cache.sqlite` | `AppSupport/` | the face-recognition cache | app |
| `validation_labels.json` | `AppSupport/` | validation labels | app |
| `cluster_names.json`, `cluster_promotions.json` | a clustering run's output folder | cluster naming and promotion decisions | app |
| `findtag-journal/`, `.findtagd.lock` | `AppSupport/` | the FindTag daemon's journal and lock (above) | `findtagd` |
| `media-person-links.json` | caller-supplied folder; none on disk | "this record is about this person" links; no caller today | app |
| `poi_profiles/`, `output/cluster_faces/`, `models/`, `photos/` | `repo/` (git-ignored) | the Python face pipeline's working folders and face models | script |
| `findtagd.log` | `Logs/` | the daemon's START/OUTCOME, one line per file | `findtagd` |
| `pf_*` (≈ 30 keys), `people.*`, `peopleMenu.*`, `PersonFinder.recentSearchPaths`, `findTag.backgroundEnabled` | `defaults` | face-pipeline settings; People tab view state; run the daemon | app |

The daemon is the app binary relaunched detached (`VideoScan --find-tag --person <name>`). The face pipeline runs in `venv/` (dlib / ArcFace / AdaFace); no cloud model (hard rule 13).

# Logs and Logging

`Logs/` is the one log sink: `<name>.log`, rotated to `<name>-<date>.log`. Every long job writes START / OUTCOME here; nothing runs silently (hard rule 5).

|---|---|---|---|
| `videoscan.log` | `Logs/` | the app's log: every MFO job's START/OUTCOME, warnings (4 MB) | app |

| `background.log` | `Logs/` | the helper's START/OUTCOME per job (not yet on disk) | helper |

*Rick's ask (2026-10-31): "a PDF of the database fields and organization of the data so I can read it and know how it is organized." Generated by `tools/data_organization.py` from the live catalog read-only — table names, columns and row counts only, no family data. Regenerate after a migration.*

## The three homes, in one paragraph

**1. `catalog.sqlite`** (App Support) is the truth: every file's identity, every decision Rick made, and every machine observation that has earned a seat — one committer, fixity, backups, rows never deleted. **2. Sidecar stores the engines own** (`audio-fingerprints.sqlite`, `model-lab.sqlite`, `metadata_cache.sqlite`) hold bulk, regenerable material the app reads directly. **3. The background helper's files** (`background/queue`, `checkpoints`, `journal/*.jsonl`) carry work in transit; the app's committer applies the journal into the catalog. `.scratch/` is the lab bench and is throwaway.

**Vocabulary.** A fact Rick set is a **decision** (`user_*`, stars, people tags, events, archive). A fact a machine produced is an **observation** — Rick's own word in the service design — carrying `provenance` / `source` (which engine, which model and prompt hash, when). A decision always outranks an observation; an observation never supports the inference that produced it.

## 2. Sidecar stores (App Support; the app reads them directly; regenerable)

| Store | Tables / columns | Keyed by | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `audio-fingerprints.sqlite` | `fingerprints` — landmarks per content digest | content digest | same-footage matching; the stamp is in `sound_prints` |
| `model-lab.sqlite` | `runs` (run_id, approach_id, revision, prompt_hash, host, model_digest, git_sha, sampler_id, started_at) · `outputs` (run_id, content_digest, size_bytes, window_start_s, window_end_s, family, raw_json, schema_valid, elapsed_s) · `segments` (content_digest, engine, start_s, end_s, text) · `vectors` (content_digest, model, window_start_s, window_end_s, dims, blob) | content digest + run | append-only (triggers forbid update/delete); every model output with its model and prompt hash |
| `metadata_cache.sqlite` | `probe_cache` (path, file_size, mod_date, stream_type, duration_seconds, dates, container, codecs, resolution, frame_rate, bitrates, color_space, bit_depth, scan_type, audio channels/sample rate, …) | path + size + mtime | the ffprobe cache: a move or a touch re-probes (cheap, by design) |
| perceptual prints | `perceptual_prints` lives IN the catalog | content digest | picture prints for same footage across transfers |

## 3. The background helper's files (`~/Library/Application Support/VideoScan/background/`)

| Path | Holds | Durability |
|---|---|---|
| `queue/<job-id>.json` | a JobRequest (kind, lane, parameters, requested-by) | atomic publish + full fsync: the app's intent survives a forced reboot |
| `checkpoints/<job-id>.json` | the last completed unit of a job | atomic publish; regenerable |
| `journal/*.jsonl` | one line per catalog-bound observation (digest, kind, value, by, evidence) | append-only; the app's committer applies it; refused lines kept with the reason |
| `~/Library/Logs/VideoScan/background.log` | START / OUTCOME per job, one line per file analyzed | log |

## 4. Where each kind of machine observation lands

| Observation | Produced by | Lands in |
|---|---|---|
| scene caption, on-screen text, burned-in date | captioner (the 8B from step 2) | `captions` + `caption_runs` (via the journal) |
| transcript | Whisper | `transcripts` |
| era / inferred date | 8B era contract, fused with the file's facts | `inferred_dates` (range_start, range_end, confidence, source, reason); v14 adds provenance assertions |
| dossier (per-file summary of the above) | DossierPropagation | `dossiers` |
| sound print / picture print | audio fingerprint engine / perceptual hash | `sound_prints` stamp + `audio-fingerprints.sqlite`; `perceptual_prints` |
| same footage / likeness / duplicates | fingerprint matching, hashes | `footage_likeness`, `footage_membership`, `duplicate_groups` / `duplicate_members` |
| media checks | integrity engines | `media_checks`, `integrity_runs` |
| raw model outputs, segments, vectors | model lab, Whisper segments, embeddings | `model-lab.sqlite` only (bulk; never the catalog) |
| people presence | face pipeline + roster + Rick's confirmations | People stores (separate by design) + `people_tags` |

## 5. Rules that shape the layout

- Identity is the whole-file SHA-256 (`content.digest`); `files` rows are sightings of that content on a volume at a path.
- Rows are never deleted: a removal is a `tombstones` row with a state; `pending_purges` and `pending_rows` are the committer's in-flight sets.
- Human facts carry `conflict` for two copies that disagree; the app shows the conflict, never picks.
- Every machine row carries `provenance` or `source`; `caption_runs` records which model captioned which digest when.
- `derived_unverified` is the quarantine for machine facts imported from the old JSON catalog that no engine has re-verified: visible, not trusted.
- Schema changes are additive, through a migration (`grdb_migrations`), and Rick approves them.
